newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bouygues, St-Gobain study unit merger.
newsitem.headline: Bouygues, St-Gobain study unit merger.

text.p: French construction group Bouygues said in a statement it and glass-maker Cie de Saint-Gobain are studying a merger of their Saur and Cise subsidiaries to create France's third largest company for public service contract management.
If the merger goes through, Bouygues and its Saur unit intend to buy 80 percent of Cise from Saint-Gobain for 2.16 billion francs ($414.1 million) in early 1997.
The new merged company would have annual turnover exceeding 12 billion francs, of which 8.6 billion would come from France, and would employ nearly 19,000 employees, Bouygues said.
Bouygues would also restructure its capital so that after the merger, it would own 83 percent of the merged company.

Bouygues would finance the deal with 810 million francs from a 1.5 billion franc bond it would issue, 800 million francs from a medium term bank loan raised by Saur, a 550 million payment agreed by Saint-Gobain to be postponed until December 31, 2001.
Saint-Gobain said in a separate statement the planned merger terms values the whole of Cise at 2.7 billion francs. ($ = 5.215 French Francs)
